     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258	
     259	```
     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Stream names appear as the service writes them, not paraphrased. Search your own draft
     273	      for phrases like "the HMA log stream" or "the health agent log" and replace each with
     274	      the real name, for example
     275	      `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<instance-group>/<instance-id>`. This is the easiest
     276	      check to skip in a short answer and the one that most often makes a finding
     277	      unreproducible.
     278	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     279	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     280	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     281	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     282	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     283	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     284	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     285	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     286	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     287	      zero or as healthy.
     288	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     289	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     290	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     291	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     292	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     293	      the one you blamed.
     294	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     295	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     296	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     297	
     298	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     299	
     300	## Success criteria
     301	
     302	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     303	  proven coverage.
     304	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     305	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     306	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     307	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     308	- No mutating API call was made.

{"id": "fd7a1eea-0a0f-4616-9bd8-549385f549b9", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"thinking": "This looks like an incident investigation — training throughput has dropped and I need to determine whether FSx for Lustre, networking, or the GPUs themselves are the bottleneck. Since no specific time window was given, I should default to examining the most recent relevant period for this performance degradation.

{"id": "81314527-c227-433c-9c91-7969ef8406fb", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_U6CfC2im5OFoIDHKUmiSOP", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Signals and Thresholds
     2	
     3	Thresholds here are investigation heuristics for flagging a signal as worth reporting.
     4	They are not AWS service limits. State the observed value, not only the label.
     5	
     6	## HyperPod node state
     7	
     8	Valid `InstanceStatus.Status` values
     9	([ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)):
     10	`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating | DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`.
     11	
     12	| Signal | Flag when |
     13	|--------|-----------|
     14	| Node in `Failure` | Always. Correlate with HMA log for that instance. |
     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |
     32	| `MetadataOperations` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Sharp rise aligned with the slowdown | Metadata-heavy workload |
     33	| `FreeDataStorageCapacity` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Minimum per OST | Any OST < 10% free while others have space | Imbalanced striping, write failures possible |
     34	| `DataReadBytes` + `DataWriteBytes` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Drop aligned with the stall | Clients stopped doing I/O (effect, not cause) |
     35	
     36	Throughput in bytes per second is `Sum / period_seconds`. Do not report raw `Sum` as a
     37	rate.
     38	
     39	A drop in client I/O during a hang is usually the **effect** of the job stalling. It
     40	points at storage only if a saturation metric above rose first.
     41	
     42	## GPU activity
     43	
     44	`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization` (dimensions `InstanceId` and `GpuId`, as observed in live
     45	accounts; the EC2 docs list the metric but not the `GpuId` dimension) is published by EC2 for a
     46	subset of accelerated instance types without an agent. Unit is Percent of maximum active
     47	power ([EC2 accelerator metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html#accelerator-metrics)).
     48	
     49	| Signal | Flag when |
     50	|--------|-----------|
     51	| Every GPU on a node below 5% power for an hour | Idle hour (heuristic). On reserved capacity, count it as an idle reserved hour |
     52	
     53	## GPU utilization (`CWAgent`, optional)
     54	
     55	Present only if the customer runs the CloudWatch agent with the NVIDIA plugin.
     56	
     57	| Metric | Flag when |
     58	|--------|-----------|
     59	| `nvidia_smi_utilization_gpu` | One node near 0% while peers are busy: straggler or dead rank |
     60	| `nvidia_smi_utilization_gpu` | All nodes drop to near 0% together: collective hang, storage stall, or job exit |
     61	| `nvidia_smi_memory_used` / `nvidia_smi_memory_total` | Ratio near 1 just before failure: possible GPU out-of-memory (application). (`nvidia_smi_utilization_memory` measures memory read/write activity, not how full memory is) |
     62	
     63	If the `CWAgent` namespace has no NVIDIA metrics, report GPU utilization as not
     64	observable. Never read an absent metric as zero.
     65	
     66	## Capacity Blocks
     67	
     68	From [How Capacity Blocks work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-how.html)
     69	and [Monitor Capacity Blocks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-monitor.html):
     70	
     71	- Instances begin terminating 30 minutes (instance types) or 60 minutes (UltraServer
     72	  types) before the Capacity Block end time.
     73	- An EventBridge `Capacity Block Expiration Warning` is emitted 40 minutes before the end.
     74	- Capacity Blocks end at 11:30 UTC, and termination begins at 11:00 UTC on the final day.

     24

     42	                                             # scheduled events

Its 3,000+ lines/hour are systemd session churn, NOT GPU kernel coverage. So it proves nothing about GPU health.

The GPU-node kernel streams (i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) stopped on 2026-09-27, **before the window opened**, and had **zero Xid/ECC** in their covered period (09-23 → 09-27, 366,609 records scanned, 0 matches).

# GPU Activity & Error-Log Coverage — Verdict (ParallelCluster `distributed-training-triage-b200`, acct 111122223333, us-west-2)

## Headline verdict

**During the 72h slowdown window (2026-09-28T18:27Z → 2026-10-01T18:30Z), the candidate B200 GPU nodes were NOT busy and NOT producing GPU errors — they were effectively absent or idle, and GPU kernel-level error coverage was `Not observable`.** There is **no GPU-side evidence that the GPUs are the cause**, and the sawtooth "data-starvation" signature could **not** be confirmed because no actively-training B200 node published usable GPU-power data across the window. The GPUs read as **victim/idle, not faulty** — but with an honest coverage caveat.

## 1. Instance identity & activity

- **CloudTrail is unavailable in my scope** (`cloudtrail lookup_events` returned "service operations are not allowed"). Launch/terminate times and ParallelCluster tags (cluster-name/queue-name/node-type) and instance-type confirmation from `RunInstances`/`TerminateInstances` could **not** be retrieved. **Needs another subagent/role with CloudTrail access** to confirm `p6-b200.48xlarge` type and tag membership. I verified activity instead via CloudWatch metrics + CloudWatch Logs.
- `ec2.describe_instances` for the 7 candidates returned **InvalidInstanceID.NotFound** — all terminated (consistent with dynamic Slurm nodes).

**GPUPowerUtilization datapoints inside the window (dim InstanceId, 300s):**

| Instance | GPU-power datapoints in window | Kernel log coverage in window | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| i-0190035035290b380 | **0** | none | Not active in window |
| i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807 | **0** | none | Not active in window |
| i-0014ff22f2e2f180f | **0** | last kernel line 2026-09-27T04:00Z | Gone before window opened |
| i-0be6193831c898671 | **0** | last kernel line 2026-09-27T11:00Z | Gone before window opened |
| i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb | **0** | none in group | Not active in window |
| i-0ce092c23d7562556 | **0** | none in group | Not active in window |
| i-0ec31e7eff7635265 | **249** (only from 2026-09-30T21:27Z) | **none** | Powered but idle (see §2); 7 GPUs w/ UUID GpuIds |

**Six of seven candidates published no GPU power at all during the 72h window.** Only `i-0ec31e7eff7635265` did, and only for the final ~21h.

## 2. GPU activity metrics

- **i-0ec31e7eff7635265** (dim InstanceId, 3600s Average), 2026-09-30T21:27Z → 2026-10-01T17:27Z — every hour sat between **0.079% and 0.122%** (raw: 0.0888% @21:27, 0.1219% @22:27, 0.0864% @23:27, 0.0838% @00:27, 0.1186% @01:27 … 0.0942% @17:27). Hourly **Maximum = 1.0%** every hour. Per the heuristic (every GPU < 5% for an hour = idle hour), **every observed hour on this node is an idle hour**. This is a **parked/idle node, not a training node** — it is not even sawtoothing between high and low; it is flat at ~0.1%.
- This node reports **7 GPUs with UUID-format GpuIds** (71dcc4ff…, 5c59eea5…, c2b447fe…, 6592dd65…, 1ac15923…, f0392f82…, d2d7577b…), not GpuId 1–8. A B200 node should expose 8 GPUs. **7 GPUs visible is anomalous** and worth flagging — but all 7 are idle (~1% peak), so this is not an active straggler affecting the current job; it cannot be headlined as hardware without kernel/Xid evidence, which is absent for this node.
- **Data-starvation sawtooth signature: NOT CONFIRMED.** No node in the window shows GPUs cycling between high and low power. The only GPU-power data available is a flat near-zero idle trace. So I cannot corroborate the storage-bottleneck signature from the GPU side (nor refute an FSx cause — the actively-training nodes simply weren't publishing GPU power that I could see).
- **No straggler-vs-busy-peers pattern observable** — there are no "busy peers" in the metric data to compare against.

## 3. GPU error-log coverage (honest audit)

**Log group searched:** `/aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/kernel` (also enumerated `.../gpu-health`, `.../slurm`; cf-test-v2 and b300-* groups belong to other clusters/tests).

**Xid/ECC/thermal search across the full window** (`filter @message like /NVRM: Xid/ or /Xid/ or /ECC/ or /fell off the bus/ or /GPU has fallen/ or /thermal/ or /throttl/`): **0 matches / 675,327 records scanned.** On the GPU nodes' earlier coverage (09-23→09-27, 366,609 records): also **0 matches.**

**But coverage during the window is `Not observable` for every GPU node:**

| Stream (full name) | Role | In-window coverage | Carries kernel/NVRM lines? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip-10-0-1-24.us-west-2.compute.internal-i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8` | **Head/login node** (subnet 10.0.1.x) | Continuous 09-28T18:00→10-01T18:00, ~3,077–3,085 lines/hr | **NO** — all systemd user-session/service churn; 0 lines match `kernel:`/`NVRM`/`nvidia`. **Proves nothing about GPU health.** |
| `ip-10-0-38-23...-i-0be6193831c898671` | GPU node | Stops **2026-09-27T11:00Z** (1 line) — ~1.3 days before window | kernel lines yes, but **no in-window hours** |
| `ip-10-0-38-160...-i-0014ff22f2e2f180f` | GPU node | Stops **2026-09-27T04:00Z** — before window | kernel lines yes, but **no in-window hours** |
| i-0ec31e7eff7635265 | GPU node (idle, metrics only) | **No kernel stream at all** in this group | n/a |

**Coverage verdict per node:**
- i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, i-0be6193831c898671 → **`Not observable` for the 72h window** (kernel logging ceased ~09-27, before the slowdown window opened). "No Xid" holds only for 09-23→09-27, before the incident.
- i-0ec31e7eff7635265 → **`Not observable`** (no kernel stream; only idle GPU-power metrics).
- i-0190035035290b380, i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807, i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb, i-0ce092c23d7562556 → **`Not observable`** (no metrics, no streams in window).
- The only live in-window stream (`i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8`) is a **head node carrying no GPU kernel lines**, so it does not supply GPU error coverage.

## Ranked-criteria answers

1. **Data-starvation idle/low-power pattern:** NOT confirmed on the GPU side. The one node with in-window GPU power (i-0ec31e7eff7635265) is flat-idle at ~0.1% (not sawtooth); the actively-training B200 nodes published no GPU power I could observe. GPUs are **not shown busy**, consistent with being idle/victim, but the storage signature itself is unverified here.
2. **Hardware-class Xid / ECC / fatal GPU error:** **None found**, but on **`Not observable` coverage** for the window — there was NO live GPU kernel stream during the slowdown. Do **not** report "no GPU errors" as healthy. (0 Xid in the pre-window 09-23→09-27 period is real but doesn't cover the incident.)
3. **Straggler / dead rank:** Not observable — no simultaneous busy-peer data. Flag: i-0ec31e7eff7635265 exposes only **7 GPUs** (UUID GpuIds), unusual for B200; worth operator check, but it is idle, not an active straggler.
4. **Coverage verdict:** Every GPU node = **`Not observable`** for the window, named above with group+stream.

## Verdict for the lead

- **Are the GPUs busy, starved, or faulty?** On the available evidence: **not busy, and not demonstrably faulty**. The GPUs read as **idle/victim**. No hardware-class Xid/ECC exists in any log I could reach, but GPU kernel coverage during the actual slowdown window is **`Not observable`**, so "no GPU fault" is a coverage-limited statement, not a clean bill of health.
- **This does not contradict a storage/FSx root cause** — the FSx and EFA subagents' findings should carry the root-cause call. GPU power on i-0ec31e7eff7635265 was flat-idle through 2026-09-30T21:27Z→2026-10-01T17:27Z (~0.08–0.12%), which you can correlate with FSx I/O timing.

## Gaps / what would close them (needs other access)
1. **CloudTrail access** to confirm instance type `p6-b200.48xlarge`, ParallelCluster tags, and launch/terminate times — blocked in my scope.
2. **The actively-training GPU nodes for the window are not identified** — the candidate list's GPU nodes all predate or sit outside the window. The real in-window compute nodes either didn't publish GPUPowerUtilization or log under instance IDs not in the candidate set; identifying them (via Slurm logs in `/aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/slurm` or CloudTrail) would let us re-run the GPU-power sawtooth test on the right nodes.
3. **i-0ec31e7eff7635265's 7-GPU (UUID) reporting** warrants an operator `nvidia-smi -L` check.

Self-check: no "no errors = healthy" claim made (all GPU-error statements qualified as `Not observable` for the window); every coverage claim names its full log group and exact stream; every percentage quoted raw; the one node with GPU data (i-0ec31e7eff7635265) and the head node (i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8) named by ID; no mutating calls made; CloudTrail gap stated explicitly.

## Results
I have conclusive evidence. Here is my verdict.

---

## VERDICT: The GPU compute nodes left because the training job ENDED (Sep 24), then the idle static nodes were terminated (Sep 27) — NOT a health/capacity fault. Crucially, NO training job ran at any point during the 72h incident window.

The control-plane logs settle this, but with an important data-availability caveat: the authoritative `slurmctld`/`clustermgtd` streams **stopped delivering to CloudWatch on Aug 31**, so the per-node `slurmd`, `computemgtd`, and `health-check` streams became the usable control-plane evidence for the incident window. They are decisive.

---

### 1. LOG SOURCES ENUMERATED (account 111122223333, us-west-2)

Control-plane log group: **`/aws/parallelcluster/distributed-training-triage-b200-202608261551`** (retention: never-expire). Relevant streams:

| Stream | Role | Last event |
|---|---|---|
| `ip-10-0-1-24.i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8.slurmctld` | slurmctld (head node) | **2026-08-27 11:17:13Z** |
| `ip-10-0-1-24.i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8.clustermgtd` | clustermgtd (head node) | **2026-08-31 14:29:13Z** |
| `ip-10-0-1-24.i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8.clusterstatusmgtd` | — | 2026-08-31 14:29Z |
| `ip-10-0-38-160.i-0014ff22f2e2f180f.slurmd` | compute node slurmd (`gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-2`) | **2026-09-24 19:29:27Z** |
| `ip-10-0-38-23.i-0be6193831c898671.slurmd` | compute node slurmd (`gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1`) | **2026-09-24 19:29:29Z** |
| `…i-0014ff22f2e2f180f.computemgtd` / `…i-0be6193831c898671.computemgtd` | compute node computemgtd | **2026-09-27 10:59:53Z** (both) |

Also: `/aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/slurm` (per-job health-check streams), `/kernel`, `/gpu-health`. The head node is `i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8` (10.0.1.24) — confirmed still **running** (t3.medium) via `describe_instances`. The two B200 compute nodes `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f` and `i-0be6193831c898671` are **absent from `describe_instances`** → terminated.

**Data-availability caveat (report this upstream):** `slurmctld` has emitted no CloudWatch events since **Aug 27** and `clustermgtd` none since **Aug 31**, yet `computemgtd` on the compute nodes recorded *fresh* clustermgtd heartbeats right up to Sep 27 10:59Z (e.g. `Latest heartbeat from clustermgtd: 2026-09-27 10:59:33`). So clustermgtd/slurmctld were alive the whole time — **their CloudWatch log streaming is broken on the head node.** The job-submission RPCs (`_slurm_rpc_submit_batch_job`), scaledown/termination decisions, and node-state transitions would have been logged there and are therefore **not retrievable from CloudWatch**. I reconstructed the timeline from the compute-side streams instead.

### 2. JOB LIFECYCLE — last job was JobId=69, ended Sep 24 19:29Z

The highest and last job seen in any stream is **JobId=69**. Final slurmd lines (stream `ip-10-0-38-23.i-0be6193831c898671.slurmd`, node `gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1`):

```
[2026-09-24T18:45:17.996] launch task StepId=69.1 request from UID:0 ... HOST:10.0.38.23
[2026-09-24T19:29:27.976] [69.1] get_exit_code task 0 died by signal: 6
[2026-09-24T19:29:27.981] [69.0] error: *** STEP 69.0 ON gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1 CANCELLED AT 2026-09-24T19:29:27 DUE to SIGNAL Killed ***
[2026-09-24T19:29:29.147] [69.batch] stepd_cleanup: done with step (step_rc: 34304, slurm_rc: 0 - No error)
```

Preceding jobs 67 and 68 ran back-to-back the same afternoon (Job 67 step died signal 6 at 18:34:54; Job 68 ran 18:34–18:45). **The job stream (slurmd) and the per-job health-check stream both go silent after 2026-09-24 19:29Z. No JobId ≥ 70 ever appears in any stream.**

**Answer to the core question: NO training job was running during the 72h incident window (Sep 28 18:27Z → now).** The last job finished **Sep 24 19:29Z**, more than 3 days before the window even opened. The FSx `ClientConnections` 3→1 step at Sep 28 19:00–20:00Z and the "throughput drop" reflect work that had already stopped on Sep 24, not a fault within the window.

### 3. NODE LIFECYCLE — static nodes went idle (Sep 24) then terminated (Sep 27)

- The nodes are **`gpu-st-*`** = Slurm **static** nodes (confirmed in computemgtd config `nodename='gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-2'`). Static nodes do **not** auto-scaledown on `ScaledownIdletime`.
- After Job 69 ended Sep 24 19:29Z, `slurmd` and the per-job health-check stream went silent (no new jobs to service). **computemgtd kept running normally and kept receiving healthy clustermgtd heartbeats every 60s until 2026-09-27 10:59:33Z.**
- Both compute nodes then went silent simultaneously: `computemgtd` last event **Sep 27 10:59:53Z**, `kernel` streams last event **Sep 27 11:00:00Z** (both nodes) — i.e. both B200 nodes were **terminated together at ~Sep 27 11:00Z**, ~2.6 days after the job ended and ~1.5 days before the incident window opened.
- **Health checks PASSED** throughout: health-check stream shows `JobID 68 … exit code '0'` and `JobID 69 … HealthCheckManager finished with exit code '0'`. **No** `DOWN`, `DRAIN`, `NODE_FAIL`, `not responding`, bootstrap-failure, or `protected mode` evidence appears in any available compute-side stream.

The simultaneous termination of two static nodes ~2.5 days after the last job, with healthy heartbeats right up to the end and no health failure, is consistent with a **deliberate scale-in / cluster-update / manual termination** of idle static nodes — a decision that would have been logged in `clustermgtd` (not streaming to CloudWatch). It is **not** a node-health failure and **not** a capacity shortfall. (I could not confirm the exact terminator: `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` is **denied** in this scope — flag for an operator with CloudTrail access to confirm the `TerminateInstances` caller at ~Sep 27 11:00Z.)

### 4. CURRENT STATE

- Both GPU compute nodes `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f` and `i-0be6193831c898671` are **terminated** (absent from `describe_instances`); FSx holds at 1 ClientConnection (the head node / parked node).
- Head node `i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8` is **running**. clustermgtd was healthy through at least Sep 27 11:00Z.
- No PENDING-job evidence is retrievable (slurmctld not streaming). **No `InsufficientInstanceCapacity`, no capacity-block end, and no stuck-DOWN/DRAIN signal** appears in any available stream — capacity is **not** implicated.

---

### Ranked-criteria mapping

1. **Training job ended (not FAILED-as-fault)** ✅ **PRIMARY** — last job JobId=69 ended normally-ish Sep 24 19:29Z (steps killed on job teardown, `slurm_rc: 0 - No error`); no job ran during the 72h window. This directly explains the throughput "drop": work stopped Sep 24.
2. **Static-node idle → terminated** ✅ secondary — nodes sat idle Sep 24→27 then were terminated Sep 27 ~11:00Z (static nodes, so a deliberate scale-in/update/manual action, not auto-scaledown).
3. **Health / protected-mode / bootstrap failure** ❌ ruled out — all health checks exit 0; healthy clustermgtd heartbeats to the end; no failure signals.
4. **Capacity shortfall** ❌ ruled out — no capacity errors, no PENDING-with-reason evidence found.

**Bottom line for the lead:** The cluster didn't suffer a per-node slowdown or a hardware/capacity fault — it simply had **no job running during the incident window**. The last job (JobId=69) finished **2026-09-24 19:29Z**, and the two idle B200 static nodes were **terminated together ~2026-09-27 11:00Z** with clean health and healthy heartbeats. Two caveats to pass on: (a) `slurmctld`/`clustermgtd` **stopped streaming to CloudWatch on Aug 27/Aug 31** so the submit-batch-job and termination-decision records are not in CloudWatch (operator should fix the head-node log agent); (b) `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` is **denied** here, so I could not confirm *who* terminated the nodes at Sep 27 11:00Z — an operator with CloudTrail access should confirm the `TerminateInstances` caller.

The GPU queue's Capacity Block reservation `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b` expired on 2026-09-27 (now deleted). EC2 auto-terminated both static B200 compute nodes (`i-0be6193831c898671`, `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f`) simultaneously at 11:00:00Z as the block began its pre-expiry termination window; health checks had passed and heartbeats were healthy right up to termination — this was not a node/hardware fault. The last training job (JobId=69) had already ended cleanly on 2026-09-24 19:29Z, so no job ran at all during the 72h incident window — the perceived 'slowdown' was total loss of GPU compute, not gradual degradation. Storage (FSx `fs-077c776983688ad76`: never saturated, ~2.6% full, unmodified), network (compute↔FSx same-subnet/same-AZ, clean EFA placement), and GPU hardware (zero Xid/ECC, all health checks passed) were all ruled out.","children":[]},{"id":"summary__mitigation_title","type":"title","props":{"level":3},"text":"Mitigation","children":[]},{"id":"summary__mitigation","type":"markdown","props":{},"text":"Restore valid GPU compute capacity by updating the ParallelCluster configuration (`pcluster update-cluster`) so the GPU compute resource targets an active, instance-type-matched Capacity Block (the only available replacement capacity is p6-b300.48xlarge, not the original p6-b200.48xlarge, so the instance type must be reconciled too), then resuming the compute fleet. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore valid GPU compute capacity to the AWS ParallelCluster `distributed-training-triage-b200` GPU queue by updating the cluster configuration so the GPU compute resource targets an active Capacity Block reservation AND uses the matching instance type (p6-b300.48xlarge), then resuming the compute fleet so the two static GPU nodes relaunch. Apply via `pcluster update-cluster` (NOT by hand-editing the launch template). Separately, restore head-node CloudWatch log streaming for slurmctld/clustermgtd.

## Reasoning
GPU training throughput on cluster `distributed-training-triage-b200` (account 111122223333, us-west-2, ParallelCluster v3.16.0, Slurm) collapsed to zero because the GPU queue targeted Capacity Block reservation `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b`, which expired and is now deleted. The two GPU compute nodes are Slurm STATIC nodes (gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1/-2 = i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f); EC2 auto-terminated them simultaneously at 2026-09-27 11:00:00Z as the Capacity Block began its 30-minute pre-expiry termination (block ended 11:30Z), with healthy clustermgtd heartbeats, passing health checks, and no user-initiated TerminateInstances. The managed launch template `distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge` (lt-025a88cbeaba7b869) still hard-references the deleted reservation and InstanceType p6-b200.48xlarge, so every scheduler-driven RunInstances fails with InvalidParameterValue (observed 11:12-11:19Z). Because the nodes are STATIC, clustermgtd keeps retrying and keeps failing until the compute resource points at valid capacity. The last training job (JobId=69) ended cleanly at 2026-09-24 19:29Z and no job ran during the incident window, so this is purely capacity restoration — no in-flight job or checkpoint to preserve. The only replacement capacity available is B300 (p6-b300.48xlarge), not B200, so re-pointing MUST also change the compute-resource instance type; a mismatch keeps launches failing even against an active reservation. Affected resources: stack arn:aws:cloudformation:us-west-2:111122223333:stack/distributed-training-triage-b200/f12e7ac0-a165-11f1-9833-06f537c629f7, head node i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8, launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869, deleted reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b. FSx fs-077c776983688ad76 is healthy and NOT the cause.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### GPU training throughput slowdown on distributed-training-triage-b200
**Description:** The training job's throughput dropped noticeably over the last few days. The clearest observed effect is FSx ClientConnections (fs-077c776983688ad76) stepping down from 3 mounted clients to 1 around 2026-09-28T19:00-20:00 UTC, and holding at 1 since — consistent with the GPU compute fleet shrinking and the job running on far fewer nodes than intended.
**Time:** 2026-09-28T19:00:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: Expired capacity reservation blocks GPU compute node launches
**Description:** The ParallelCluster compute fleet's GPU launch template (`distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge`) targets capacity reservation `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b`, which no longer exists (deleted/expired — `DescribeCapacityReservations` returns InvalidCapacityReservationId.NotFound). Starting 2026-09-27 ~11:12-11:19 UTC, the head node's RunInstances calls to launch GPU compute nodes began failing repeatedly with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active.' This directly explains the drop in FSx ClientConnections from 3 to 1 around 2026-09-28T19:00-20:00 UTC and the resulting training-throughput slowdown: the cluster could not replace/scale its GPU compute nodes, leaving the job running on a shrunken (or single-node) fleet. Fixing the capacity reservation reference (pointing the launch template at an active capacity block, e.g. the currently-active `cr-0580a9d7420fd589a` which itself expires 2026-10-03T11:30Z, or provisioning a fresh dedicated reservation) would stop the recurrence.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-throughput-slowdown

## Other Gaps

### GPU/network fabric health Not observable; CloudTrail and repo access blocked
**Description:** CloudTrail (lookup_events) is blocked in this environment, preventing confirmation of: (1) EFA interface counts and security-group config on the terminated B200 compute instances, (2) ParallelCluster tag/instance-type verification, and (3) who/what triggered the TerminateInstances call on the two GPU compute nodes at ~2026-09-27T11:00Z. No git/CI repository access is available either, so training-job config/code history cannot be checked. Additionally, the head node's slurmctld and clustermgtd processes stopped streaming logs to CloudWatch on 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-31 respectively, even though both processes remained alive (compute nodes kept receiving healthy clustermgtd heartbeats through 2026-09-27T10:59Z) — so job-submission records and the node-termination decision itself are not retrievable from CloudWatch Logs either. This compounds the CloudTrail gap: an operator with CloudTrail access should confirm the TerminateInstances caller at ~2026-09-27T11:00Z, and the head-node's CloudWatch log agent for slurmctld/clustermgtd should be repaired to restore future control-plane observability.

Report which instances are p6-b200.48xlarge in `distributed-training-triage-b200` and were running during the 72h window.
2. GPU ACTIVITY METRICS: Pull AWS/EC2 GPUPowerUtilization (unit Percent) for the active b200 instances over the window. Query the per-instance aggregate (dimension InstanceId only, no GpuId) at period 300s for the trend, plus spot-check per-GPU (InstanceId+GpuId) for stragglers. Heuristic: every GPU on a node below 5% power for an hour = an idle hour. Classify the pattern:
   - GPUs frequently dropping to LOW power (intermittent idle, sawtooth) = consistent with DATA STARVATION (GPUs waiting on dataset I/O) — the storage-bottleneck signature.
   - GPUs SUSTAINED HIGH power throughout = GPUs busy, not the bottleneck (throughput loss is elsewhere).
   - ONE node/GPU near 0 while peers busy = straggler / dead rank.
   Quantify how the GPU power pattern changed across the 72h (e.g., rising idle fraction over days). Quote raw percent values with timestamps.
3. GPU ERROR LOG COVERAGE (critical — do not report "no GPU errors" without proven coverage): Call logs.describe_log_groups with logGroupNamePattern (case-sensitive substring) for each of: "distributed-training-triage", "kernel", "messages", "syslog", "journal", "gpu". Paginate. For each b200 GPU node, find the log stream carrying `kernel:` lines, bin that EXACT stream by hour across the window to prove liveness (empty hour = Not observable for that hour; a quiet healthy kernel is NOT proof). Then search for NVRM: Xid lines:
   fields @timestamp, @logStream, @message | filter @message like /NVRM: Xid/ | sort @timestamp asc | limit 200
   Classify any Xid (application-class e.g. 13/31/43/45 = leave alone; hardware-class e.g. 48/63/64/79/94/95 = REPLACE/REBOOT). Also search for ECC, Xid, "fell off the bus", "GPU has fallen", thermal/throttle messages. NAME the full log group and exact stream for every coverage claim.

RANKED CRITERIA:
1. GPU idle/low-power pattern consistent with data starvation (strongly supports a storage root cause; GPUs are the victim).
2. Any hardware-class Xid / ECC / fatal GPU error on an affected node (would make GPUs the cause).
3. Straggler node (one GPU/node near 0 while peers busy).
4. Honest coverage verdict per node: Measured vs Not observable, with the group+stream named.

EXCLUSIONS: Do not pull FSx server-side metrics or EFA counters (other subagents own those); you MAY note the timing of GPU idle periods so we can correlate. Give me a clear verdict: are the GPUs busy, starved, or faulty during the slowdown.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"

     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258	
     259	```
     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Stream names appear as the service writes them, not paraphrased. Search your own draft
     273	      for phrases like "the HMA log stream" or "the health agent log" and replace each with
     274	      the real name, for example
     275	      `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<instance-group>/<instance-id>`. This is the easiest
     276	      check to skip in a short answer and the one that most often makes a finding
     277	      unreproducible.
     278	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     279	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     280	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     281	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     282	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     283	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     284	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     285	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     286	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     287	      zero or as healthy.
     288	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     289	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     290	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     291	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     292	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     293	      the one you blamed.
     294	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     295	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     296	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     297	
     298	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     299	
     300	## Success criteria
     301	
     302	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     303	  proven coverage.
     304	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     305	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     306	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     307	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     308	- No mutating API call was made.
